name: 16b retrieval versus full context cost
title: Cost of one question with the full filing or six retrieved chunks
subtitle: Reference 7B in bf16 on one H100; prefill at 40% of 989 TFLOP/s, decode limited by 3.35 TB/s; 200-token answer

steps.caption: One question about net debt. The full filing puts 96,000 tokens in the prompt, while retrieval puts in six chunks of 1,000 tokens, 6,000 in all. Both write a 200-token answer on one H100.
Prefill of the full filing costs 3.71 x 10^15 FLOPs, 1.29 x 10^15 for the weights and 2.42 x 10^15 for attention, which is 9.38 seconds. The six chunks cost 9.0 x 10^13 FLOPs, 0.23 seconds.
The cache holds 0.5 MiB per token: 50.3 GB for the filing beside 13.5 GB of weights, so one request fills the GPU. The six chunks need 3.1 GB, room for 21 such requests.
Each decode step reads the weights and the whole cache: 63.8 GB, or 19.0 ms, for the filing against 16.6 GB, or 5.0 ms, for the chunks. The 200-token answer takes 3.81 against 0.99 seconds.
In total the question costs 13.2 GPU-seconds with the full filing and 1.2 with retrieval, about 11 times more, and the long request also keeps the whole GPU to itself.
Retrieval can miss evidence. If each of the three passages is retrieved with probability 0.8, all three arrive together only 0.8^3 = 0.51 of the time, while the full filing always contains them.
